title: Affine-line purity
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $Y$ be the scheme of the
affine-line datum and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda=A$. The affine-line purity
comparison $\gamma_{p,K}$ of
[def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison] – the adjoint of the
projection-formula composite
$Rp_!Lp^*K(1)[2]\cong K\otimes^L Rp_!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\to K$
formed with the projective-line trace and normalized by the orientation
$\operatorname{pur}_s$ of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] – is an isomorphism

$$
\gamma_{p,K}:Lp^*K(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp^!K.
$$

It is natural in $K$ and compatible with arbitrary base change of $Y$.
(Source: the relative affine-line case of cohomological purity, as in
Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 16, Theorems 16.1 and
16.7 and Proposition 16.11, with the acyclicity computation of Example
16.3 and the Gysin sequence of the divisor, over an arbitrary base
scheme.)

On the ordinary etale site, [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction] constructs $Rp_!\dashv p^*(1)[2]$ by composing $j_!\da

proof.text: Put $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$ and $a:X\hookrightarrow P$, so $p=qa$. The standard chart is open by [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion], and $q$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. The datum [def-pur-affine-line-datum] gives $Y$ separated finite type over $k$; the polynomial charts make $X,P$ finite type over $k$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y,X,P$ Noetherian; in particular $a$ is quasi-compact. Applied to $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] gives $d\geq0$ with $\dim P\leq d$, since its unique fibre is $P$. These verify the compactification and dimension hypotheses of the actual-adjoint comparison. The same statements apply over every separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y'$ in the chapter setting.

source.place: Proof, coefficient comparison sentence: compactification and finite dimension

proof.text: The datum gives $A=A_{E,n}$, $e\mid n$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Put $r=n/e$ and $m=\ell^r$. By [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level], $mA=0$ and the specified twist is the finite roots-of-unity twist; $m$ is invertible on every scheme in Step 1. Its ordinary etale representative $B_T=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{m,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A_T$ is locally constant and free of rank one by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The finite-ring origin equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] gives $K_0\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\alpha:C_YK_0\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, where $C_T=\nu_T^*$. The Tor-reflection clause of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] gives $K_0$ the same finite Tor interval as $K$. Hence $K_0\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

source.place: Proof, coefficient comparison sentence: ordinary etale finite-Tor witness

proof.text: For $p,q,a$, [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] preserves bounded constructibility and the finite Tor interval. The inverse-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies the pullbacks of the witness of Step 2; [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] reflects their Tor intervals onto these ordinary etale representatives. For $p$, [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], applied to the trivial rank-one bundle, supplies the canonical endpoint isomorphism $C_X(p_{\mathrm{et}}^*K_0\otimes_A^LB_X[2])\cong Lp^*K(1)[2]$, natural in the witness. Tensoring with $B_X$ preserves the cohomological and Tor intervals because it is locally $A_X$ by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; the shift $[2]$ subtracts two from their endpoints. Thus both representatives of this source are in $D^b_{ctf}$. No exceptional-image preservation is used.

source.place: Proof, coefficient comparison sentence: pullback and twisted-source hypotheses

proof.text:
Work first on the ordinary etale sites, where inverse image for constant coefficients is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so $Lp^*=p^*$ and $Lq^*=q^*$. Set $T_P=A_P(1)[2]$, $T_X=a^*T_P$, $G_q(L)=q^*L\otimes_A^LT_P$, and $G_p(L)=a^*G_q(L)=p^*L(1)[2]$. By [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], $Rq_*\dashv G_q$ with actual counit $\epsilon_{q,L}=(1_L\otimes t_q)\pi_q^{-1}$. By [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], $Da_!\dashv a^*$ on the entire ordinary derived categories; denote its evaluation counit by $e_a$. The compactification formula [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $F_p=Rq_*Da_!$. Compose these two adjunctions using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. It gives $F_p\dashv G_p$ with actual counit
$$\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,L}=\epsilon_{q,L}\circ Rq_*(e_{a,G_qL}):Rq_*Da_!a^*G_qL\longrightarrow L.$$
Thus the adjunction includes its counit, not just the existence of a right adjoint.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: compose the open and normalized projective-line adjunctions

proof.text:
Identify this counit at $L=K_0$. Let $u:Da_!T_X\to T_P$ be $e_{a,T_P}$ and put $\int_p=t_q\circ Rq_*u$. Write $\rho:Da_!a^*(q^*K_0\otimes^LT_P)\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*K_0\otimes^LDa_!T_X$ for the inverse open projection map, with the tensor symmetry understood. Its invertibility is the case $f=a$ of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]; the same node for $f=p$ gives the compact-support projection isomorphism. The open evaluation satisfies
$$e_{a,q^*K_0\otimes T_P}=(1_{q^*K_0}\otimes u)\rho.$$
Indeed the counit of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] is identity on every etale test object factoring through $X$; on such an object the displayed equation sends $x\otimes t$ to $x\otimes t$, and on the zero-extension presheaf's other components both maps are zero. Choose K-flat representatives with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The same equality holds in each bidegree of their tensor complexes, and the maps respect the tensor differentials, so it gives the asserted equality for derived tensor. No equality of unspecified isomorphisms is being assumed. By the compactification definition of the projection map [def-exchange-projection], its inverse at $T_X,K_0$ is $\pi_q(Da_!T_X)^{-1}\circ Rq_*\rho$. Naturality of the proper projection isomorphism [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] with respect to $u$ therefore gives
$$\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,K_0}=(1_{K_0}\otimes t_q)\pi_q(T_P)^{-1}Rq_*(1\otimes u)Rq_*\rho
=(1_{K_0}\otimes\int_p)\pi_q(Da_!T_X)^{-1}Rq_*\rho.$$
This is precisely the projection-formula integration composite defining the comparison in [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison].

source.place: Proof, second sentence: calculate the actual composite counit as projection-formula integration

proof.text: Let $p^\times$ be the ordinary etale right adjoint supplied by [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] for the fixed compactification $(a,q)$. Compare $F_p\dashv G_p$ of Step 4 with $F_p\dashv p^\times$. Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to the identity isomorphism of their common left adjoint $F_p$. Its conjugate $\delta:G_p\xrightarrow{\sim}p^\times$ is a natural isomorphism, and its component $\delta_{K_0}$ is the transpose of $\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,K_0}$ under $F_p\dashv p^\times$ (the formula for the conjugate is the unit followed by the image of this counit). Step 5 identifies that counit with integration. Consequently it is the specified comparison, rather than merely some isomorphism between the same two objects, that is invertible on the etale site. Naturality is also obtained here from the natural transformation $\delta$.

source.place: Proof, third sentence: uniqueness of right adjoints with the specified counit

proof.text: Transport the ordinary adjunction to the pro-etale site on the bounded-below witness. [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] identifies $P(C_XM)$ with $C_Y(FM)$ for every bounded-below etale-origin $M$, and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies $R\nu_{Y,*}C_YK_0$ with $K_0$. The Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] therefore identifies the right adjoint $H=C_Xp^\times R\nu_{Y,*}$ with the transported ordinary right adjoint. Exact comparison pullback [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] and the ringed-topos tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identify the source with $Lp^*K(1)[2]$ using the twist comparison in [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. The endpoint identifications are natural in $K_0$ and in the witness.

source.place: Proof, fourth sentence: realize the actual adjunction on the pro-etale site

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] with $S=Y$, the trivial rank-one bundle $p:X\to Y$ and $K_0$ of Step 2. Its restricted projective-line trace and projection-map clauses identify the ordinary integration composite of Step 5 with the actual $a_K$ of [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. Its final transpose formula states $\eta^p_{C_YK_0}=C_X(\eta^e_{K_0})$, under the endpoint isomorphism of Step 3 and $C_Xp^\times K_0\cong Rp^!C_YK_0$. By Step 6, $\eta^e_{K_0}=\delta_{K_0}$. Therefore the specified $\gamma_{p,K}$ is $C_X(\delta_{K_0})$ conjugated by those endpoint isomorphisms and $\alpha$. It is an isomorphism. Naturality follows from this formula, the naturality of $\delta$ and the natural witness comparisons; the bounded-below site-comparison unit and full faithfulness of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] make the formula independent of the witness. The target is in $D^b_{ctf}$ because it is isomorphic to the source of Step 3. This uses the cited relative etale-origin transpose formula, not an ambient pro-etale adjunction.

source.place: Proof, actual-adjoint comparison sentence: apply the existing integration-transpose comparison

proof.text:
Check the orientation normalization. Let $D_0=s(Y)$, viewed also as the zero-section divisor in $P$. Its equations on the standard two affine charts are $t$ and $1$, so the dual ideal generators have transition $t^{-1}$; thus $\mathcal O_P(D_0)=\mathcal O_P(1)$ with the transition convention used in the projective-line class. This follows directly from [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. The supported Kummer morphism of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] for this Cartier divisor, after forgetting supports, is therefore $h=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$. On $X$ it is the boundary of the coordinate $t$, and [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] identifies its finite-coefficient realization with the same supported morphism on the pro-etale site. This is the boundary defining $\operatorname{pur}_s$ in [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. The trace of [def-amb-p1-trace] satisfies $t_qh=1$. Hence $\int_p$ sends the image of this supported orientation to $1$. For the proper zero section, the identity-open compactification in [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $Rs_!=Rs_*$. The canonical composition of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and $ps=\mathrm{id}$ then give $Rp_!Rs_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ on these etale-origin inputs. Composing the two Hom bijections for the zero section and projection, using the composite-counit formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and $ps=\mathrm{id}$, identifies this evaluation with
$$\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\operatorname{pur}_s}Rs^!\Lambda_X(1)[2]\xrightarrow{Rs^!\gamma_{p,\Lambda}}Rs^!Rp^!\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_Y.$$
It is the identity, which verifies the stated normalization without multiplying the comparison by an unspecified unit.

source.place: Statement, normalization by the orientation; original sk-prop-an Step 5(d): Kummer class of the zero-section divisor

proof.text:
Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be an arbitrary morphism in the chapter's fixed setting, and write $g_X:X'\to X$, $g_P:P'\to P$, $a',q',p'$ for the pulled-back compactification. Here $Y'$ is again a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, as required by the chapter setting; $g$ is any $k$-morphism between these schemes. No flatness, smoothness, or etaleness is required of $g$. For $L$ bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, all arguments of the following exchange maps are bounded below. On these ordinary etale inputs let $C_p:g^*F_p\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{p'}g_X^*$ be the compact-support exchange and $\tau_L:g_X^*G_pL\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{p'}g^*L$ the pullback/twist identification. The isomorphy of $C_p$ on these bounded-below inputs is [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]; the open $a$ is quasi-compact because $P$ is Noetherian. Use the actual compactification formula in [def-cbc-exchange-map]: proper exchange for $q$, followed by open-extension exchange for $a$. The latter is the inverse of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], applied degreewise using [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. The trace and projective-line adjunction normalization commute with base change by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. The root-of-unity twist comparison is [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The projection transformations commute with the proper exchange by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]; the open evaluation commutes with pullback because its maps are the identity on the open and zero off it, as specified in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Substituting these identities into the explicit counit formula of Step 4 yields the typed equality
$$g^*\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,L}=\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p',g^*L}\circ F_{p'}(\tau_L)\circ C_{p,G_pL}.$$
In particular this checks compatibility of the actual integration counit, not only of the two functors up to isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, final base-change sentences: check the defining counit before taking mates

proof.text:
Take mates of the equality in Step 10. Changing from the explicit adjunctions to the ordinary exceptional adjunctions through $\delta,\delta'$ is licensed by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. If $\beta^e_{p,g}:g_X^*p^\times\to p'^\times g^*$ is the mate of $C_p^{-1}$, its definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is the transpose of $g^*\epsilon^\times_{p,L}\circ C_{p,p^\times L}^{-1}$. The argument $p^\times L$ is bounded below by Step 6. Transposing both sides and using Step 10 and the counit compatibility of $\delta$ gives
$$\beta^e_{p,g,L}\circ g_X^*\delta_L=\delta'_{g^*L}\circ\tau_L.$$
The adjunction bijection makes equality of these transposes equality of the displayed maps.

source.place: Proof, final base-change sentences: ordinary mate of the verified counit identity

proof.text:
Use [lem-pur-exceptional-mate-site-comparison] at $f=p$, the compactification $(a,q)$ and its pullback. Step 1 verifies its geometry and dimension assumptions over $Y,Y'$; Step 6 identifies $p^\times K_0$ and $p'^\times g^*K_0$ with the bounded twisted pullbacks. The lemma identifies the actual pro-etale exceptional mate with $C_{X'}(\beta^e_{p,g,K_0})$ under its specified endpoint comparisons. The twist comparisons of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] commute with inverse image, so applying $C_{X'}$ to Step 11 and using Step 8 over $Y,Y'$ gives
$$\beta_{p,g,K}\circ Lg_X^*\gamma_{p,K}=\gamma_{p',Lg^*K}\circ\tau_K.$$
Here $g^*K_0$ witnesses $Lg^*K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] places this input in $D^b_{ctf}$. The two $\gamma$ maps are isomorphisms by Steps 1--8 over the respective bases, as is $\tau_K$. Thus the equation also proves that $\beta_{p,g,K}$ is invertible. This is arbitrary base-change compatibility in the chapter setting.

\gamma_{p,K}:Lp^*K(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp^!K.
$$

It is natural in $K$ and compatible with arbitrary base change of $Y$.

proof.text:
On the ordinary etale site, [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction]
constructs $Rp_!\dashv p^*(1)[2]$ by composing
$j_!\dashv j^*$ with the explicit projective-line adjunction.
Its counit is exactly the composite in
[def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison], since
[def-amb-p1-trace] defines the same normalized trace.
Uniqueness of a right adjoint with its counit therefore identifies its
adjoint $\gamma_{p,K}$ with an isomorphism.
The actual-adjoint comparison of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]
and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] transport this statement and
the adjunction bijection to the finite etale-origin coefficients of
this chapter. Naturality follows from the defining adjunction.
For base change, [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] identifies the mate
of compact-support base change with the inverse-image and twist
identification for this explicit affine-line adjunction. Hence the
same defining counit, and therefore $\gamma_{p,K}$, commutes with
arbitrary base change. General smooth purity is not an input here.
